title: The CEO Who Sold 'Eternal' Lightbulbs That Exploded After 100 Hours
hook: A lightbulb that never burns out sounds impossible, so this CEO made sure his 'eternal' bulbs didn't last long enough for you to notice the lie.
why_this_can_go_viral: Planned obsolescence is a universally hated concept, and the idea of a CEO intentionally making a 'forever' product deadly is darkly ironic.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Parking Lot—Then Made Your Car Vanish
hook: You park, you pay, you return to an empty space — the parking monopoly didn't steal your car, it just made you question your sanity.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone has a parking horror story, but the idea of a company systematically towing your car to a secret lot to charge a ransom is infuriating and fascinating.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Rocket Fuel Formula by Smelling a Scientist's Sweater
hook: A single sniff of a discarded sweater revealed the secret to a classified rocket propellant — and nobody ever suspected the nose.
why_this_can_go_viral: The absurd specificity of the method (smelling a sweater!) creates a powerful curiosity gap, making viewers desperate to know how it worked.

title: The Chemical Company That Sold 'Pure' Water—It Was Just Poison From Their Own Factory

why_this_can_go_viral: The betrayal of trust is extreme and deeply relatable; viewers love to hate a corporation that literally poisons its own customers.

title: The Market Manipulator Who Bought a Mountain—Then Sold the Sky

why_this_can_go_viral: The concept of selling 'the sky' is absurd and instantly conjures images of a villain from a heist movie.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Brain-Boosting' Pills—They Were Just Ground-Up Antidepressants
hook: A 'cognitive enhancement' startup was secretly selling repackaged antidepressants, making users feel smarter when they were just sedated.
why_this_can_go_viral: The wellness industry is a massive target of skepticism, and this reveals a terrifyingly plausible deception.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Dairy Farm—Then Made Milk Curdle on Purpose
hook: Milk spoiled in days, not weeks — because the monopoly engineered a bacteria into the supply chain to force you to buy more.
why_this_can_go_viral: Food spoilage is a universal frustration, and the reveal that it's intentional would spark outrage and massive sharing.

title: The Trader Who Faked a Meteorite Strike—Then Bought All the Insurance Stocks
hook: He hired a plane to drop a fake meteorite into a farm field, then shorted insurance stocks when the 'space rock' panic hit.
why_this_can_go_viral: The audacity of faking a cosmic event for financial gain is so ridiculous it feels like a movie plot, driving massive curiosity.

title: The Supplier That Sold 'Cashmere' Sweaters—They Were Made From Shredded Plastic Bags
hook: Luxury cashmere that felt 'soft' for a week — until it started shedding microplastics and your skin turned red.
why_this_can_go_viral: Fashion fraud is a huge topic, and the specific image of wearing a shredded plastic bag as a 'luxury' item is deeply satisfying to expose.

title: The CEO Who Sold 'Anti-Aging' Cream—It Was Acid That Peeled Your Skin Off
hook: A 'miracle' anti-aging cream made wrinkles disappear because it was literally dissolving the top layer of your skin — permanently.
why_this_can_go_viral: Beauty product horror stories are incredibly viral, and the grotesque detail of acid-peeling is unforgettable.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Microphone Design by Recording a Factory's Echo
hook: He placed a single recording device outside a factory, analyzed the echo, and reverse-engineered a classified microphone from the sound of its own production.
why_this_can_go_viral: The method sounds like science fiction, making it highly shareable as 'the coolest spy trick you've never heard of'.

title: The Ad That Made You Think Your Food Was Rotting—Then Sold You 'Freshness' Stickers

why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of being psychologically tricked into buying a 'solution' to a problem they created is a perfect example of dark marketing.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Airline—Then Made Seats Shrink Every Year
hook: Seat width decreased by half an inch annually for a decade, and the monopoly blamed 'new safety regulations' that didn't exist.
why_this_can_go_viral: Flying is universally miserable, and this reveals a systematic, cynical plan to make it worse — guaranteed engagement.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Mind-Controlled' Drones—They Were Just Piloted by a Guy in a Van
hook: A startup demoed drones that 'obeyed your thoughts' — but there was a man in a van with a joystick watching your brainwaves.
why_this_can_go_viral: It's a Theranos-level deception with a hilarious twist — the 'AI' was just a guy in a van.

title: The Trader Who Paid a DJ to Play a Secret Code—Then Moved a Commodity Market

why_this_can_go_viral: The crossover between nightlife and high finance is thrilling, and the idea of a secret code in a song is instantly intriguing.

title: The Oil Company That Invented a 'Green' Fuel—It Was Just Gasoline Dyed Green
hook: They sold 'eco-friendly' fuel at a premium — it was the same gasoline, just with food coloring and a new marketing slogan.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Billion-Dollar Algorithm by Watching a Janitor's Keystrokes
hook: A janitor cleaned the office every night — but the spy read the oil patterns on the keys to reconstruct a secret trading algorithm.

title: The Ad That Made You Believe Your Shower Was Dirty—Then Sold You 'Antimicrobial' Water
hook: The ad showed 'magnified' images of your shower water filled with monsters — the 'monsters' were just dust particles made to look scary.
why_this_can_go_viral: Creating fake fear to sell a useless product is a classic dark marketing tactic that viewers love to dissect.

title: The Pharmaceutical Giant That Sold 'Miracle' Weight Loss Gum—It Made Your Jaw Lock
hook: The gum was laced with a muscle relaxant that 'reduced appetite' by making it painful to open your mouth.
why_this_can_go_viral: The grotesque body horror of a locked jaw combined with a weight loss scam is deeply shocking and memorable.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI-Driven' Stock Picks—It Was Just a Random Number Generator
hook: The 'AI' consistently beat the market — because the founder just deleted the losing trades from the reports.
why_this_can_go_viral: The simplicity of the fraud (delete losses, report wins) is both hilarious and enraging, and perfectly captures startup hubris.

title: The Trader Who Bought a Dictionary—Then Sold Every Word as a 'Trademark'

title: The Spy Who Stole a Battery Formula by Dissecting a Lost Prototype Watch

why_this_can_go_viral: The forensic method (dissolving in acid) sounds like a villain move, making it incredibly shareable.

title: The Chemical Company That Sold 'Eco-Friendly' Dry Cleaning—It Burned Holes in Your Lungs

why_this_can_go_viral: The casual trade-off (cheaper solvent vs. human health) is a stark example of corporate nihilism that generates strong emotional reactions.
